definition: Migratory restlessness is a seasonal period in migratory birds when activity and responding increase as migration approaches or occurs. In the source, this state in White-crowned Sparrows was linked with markedly reduced sleep compared with non-migratory periods.

reasons: The requested field is not defensible from the packet: the source is about avian migratory behavior and sleep, not the psychology/counselling sense of learning.

The definition adds a general characterization (“seasonal period in migratory birds when activity and responding increase as migration approaches or occurs”) that is only partly supported; the packet supports increased responding and reduced sleep during a migratory period, but does not itself define the term in that general form.

The definition’s first sentence makes a general claim that migratory restlessness is a “seasonal period” in “migratory birds” with activity/responding increasing “as migration approaches or occurs”; the packet only describes this in White-crowned Sparrows and does not explicitly support the “as migration approaches” phrasing or the broader cross-species/general definition.
